answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because oasis only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, grove is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
